name: Mirissa Beach
description: A crescent-shaped bay on the south coast fringed with coconut palms, popular for its relaxed surf-town atmosphere and turquoise water. One of the best places in the world for blue whale watching during peak season.
accessibility: Easy - accessible by road and rail
significance_or_activities: Whale and dolphin watching, surfing, sunbathing, beachside dining

name: Unawatuna Beach
description: A sheltered horseshoe-shaped bay near Galle Fort with calm, swimmable water most of the year. A lively strip of bars, cafes and guesthouses lines the shore, making it one of the most visited beaches on the south coast.
accessibility: Easy - short drive from Galle town
significance_or_activities: Swimming, snorkeling, beach relaxation, nightlife

name: Hikkaduwa Beach
description: A long, lively beach on the southwest coast with a coral reef just offshore, known as one of the original surf hubs of Sri Lanka. Resident sea turtles frequently come close to shore near the harbour area.
accessibility: Easy - accessible by road and rail
significance_or_activities: Surfing, snorkeling, glass-bottom boat tours, turtle watching

name: Polhena Beach
description: A calm, shallow, reef-protected beach centrally located near Matara town, well known for allowing visitors to swim alongside wild sea turtles that favour its still waters.
accessibility: Easy - close to Matara town centre
significance_or_activities: Swimming with wild turtles, snorkeling

name: Tangalle Beach
description: A long stretch of soft-sand coastline with a quieter, less commercial feel than the beaches further west. Nearby Rekawa Beach hosts a well-known turtle conservation project.
accessibility: Moderate - further from main tourist hubs
significance_or_activities: Relaxation, turtle conservation visits, coastal walks

name: Hiriketiya Beach
description: A small horseshoe-shaped cove tucked away from the main coastal road, popular with surfers and known for its peaceful, secluded jungle-fringed setting.
accessibility: Moderate - down a quiet access road
significance_or_activities: Surfing, swimming, yoga retreats

name: Nilaveli Beach
description: A long, calm, shallow-water beach on the northeast coast, and the main gateway for boat trips to Pigeon Island Marine National Park for snorkeling among coral reefs, turtles and reef sharks.
accessibility: Easy - accessible by road
significance_or_activities: Sunbathing, swimming, boat trips to Pigeon Island, snorkeling

name: Bentota Beach
description: A wide, resort-lined beach on the west coast at the mouth of the Bentota River, known for water sports and luxury hotels designed in the tropical-modernist style pioneered by architect Geoffrey Bawa.
accessibility: Easy - close to Colombo
significance_or_activities: Jet skiing, banana boating, river safaris, resort stays

name: Arugam Bay
description: A world-renowned surf break on the east coast, drawing international surfers for its long right-hand point break, alongside a growing backpacker and yoga scene.
accessibility: Moderate - remote east coast location
significance_or_activities: Surfing, yoga, beach camping

name: Dickwella Beach
description: A calm, quiet beach on the south coast, less crowded than nearby Mirissa or Unawatuna, with a laid-back atmosphere and nearby coworking spaces.
accessibility: Easy - along the southern coastal road
significance_or_activities: Swimming, relaxation, coastal walks

name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic (Sri Dalada Maligawa)
description: A UNESCO World Heritage Buddhist temple within the former royal palace complex of the Kingdom of Kandy, believed to house a tooth relic of the Buddha. It is one of the most sacred pilgrimage sites in the Buddhist world and the focal point of the annual Esala Perahera festival.
accessibility: Easy - located in Kandy city centre
significance_or_activities: Buddhist pilgrimage site, royal palace architecture, museum, evening rituals (puja)

name: Dambulla Cave Temple (Golden Temple of Dambulla)
description: The largest and best-preserved cave temple complex in Sri Lanka, a UNESCO World Heritage Site comprising five caves with over 150 Buddha statues and extensive ceiling and wall murals dating back over two thousand years.
accessibility: Moderate - 20 minute uphill walk; not wheelchair accessible
significance_or_activities: Buddhist cave art, ancient murals, pilgrimage

name: Sigiriya Rock Fortress
description: A 5th-century rock fortress and palace ruin rising about 200 metres above the surrounding plain, often called the 'Eighth Wonder of the World'. Famous for its ancient frescoes, the Mirror Wall with historic inscriptions, and sweeping summit views.
accessibility: Challenging - steep climb with stairways to the summit
significance_or_activities: UNESCO World Heritage Site, ancient frescoes, royal palace ruins, panoramic viewpoint

name: Galle Fort
description: A fortified coastal city originally built by the Portuguese and extensively expanded by the Dutch in the 17th century, now a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Known for its cobbled streets, colonial architecture, ramparts, boutique shops and cafes.
accessibility: Easy - walkable town centre
significance_or_activities: Colonial architecture, sea rampart walks, boutique shopping, sunset views

name: Polonnaruwa Ancient City
description: The well-preserved ruins of Sri Lanka's second ancient capital, a UNESCO World Heritage Site featuring royal palaces, temples, and the Gal Vihara rock-cut Buddha statues, best explored by bicycle.
accessibility: Easy to moderate - large site
significance_or_activities: Medieval royal ruins, Gal Vihara Buddha statues, ancient reservoir (Parakrama Samudra)

name: Anuradhapura Sacred City
description: Sri Lanka's first ancient capital and a UNESCO World Heritage Site, home to enormous ancient stupas including the Ruwanwelisaya, along with monastery ruins spanning over a thousand years of history.
accessibility: Moderate - large site spread over several kilometres
significance_or_activities: Ancient Buddhist stupas, monastery ruins, sacred Bo tree

name: Ridi Viharaya (Silver Temple)
description: A 2nd-century BCE Buddhist cave temple complex said to mark the site where silver ore was discovered, funding the construction of the Ruwanwelisaya stupa in Anuradhapura. Known for its unusual mix of Kandyan and colonial architectural elements.
accessibility: Moderate - rural location off main routes
significance_or_activities: Ancient cave shrines, historic Buddha statues, quiet pilgrimage site

name: Kelaniya Raja Maha Vihara
description: A major Buddhist temple on the banks of the Kelani River near Colombo, believed to have been visited by the Buddha himself. Notable for its vivid modern murals depicting Buddhist history and the annual Duruthu Perahera festival.
accessibility: Easy - close to Colombo
significance_or_activities: Buddhist pilgrimage, murals, riverside setting

name: Jetavanaramaya Stupa
description: One of the tallest ancient brick structures in the world, this monumental stupa was once part of a large monastic complex in the sacred city of Anuradhapura and reflects the engineering achievements of ancient Sri Lanka.
accessibility: Moderate - part of larger Anuradhapura site
significance_or_activities: Ancient brick stupa, monastic ruins, archaeological significance

name: Galle Fort Lighthouse
description: A working lighthouse on the ramparts of Galle Fort, rebuilt in the early 20th century after a fire destroyed the original, and now one of the most photographed landmarks within the fort.
accessibility: Easy - within Galle Fort
significance_or_activities: Colonial-era landmark, coastal viewpoint, photography spot
